mainEntity.name: What macro split should I use?

acceptedAnswer.text: A 30/30/40 (protein/fat/carb) split is a common general-purpose starting point, but ideal splits vary by goal — higher protein for muscle building, higher fat for some low-carb approaches.

mainEntity.name: What if my percentages don't add up to 100%?

acceptedAnswer.text: Adjust the values so protein, fat, and carb percentages sum to 100% for the gram targets to match your total calorie goal exactly.

mainEntity.name: Which macro is most important to prioritize?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most nutrition guidance prioritizes protein intake first for muscle maintenance and satiety, then allows more flexibility in balancing fat and carbohydrate based on personal preference and performance.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to hit my macros exactly every day?

acceptedAnswer.text: Being consistently close over time matters more than hitting exact numbers daily — small day-to-day variation is normal and generally doesn't meaningfully affect results.

mainEntity.name: Should my macro percentages change if I'm trying to lose fat?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many people increase protein percentage during fat loss to help preserve muscle mass, often to 35-40% of total calories, adjusting fat and carbs accordingly.

mainEntity.name: What are the recommended macro ranges for adults?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Acceptable Macronutrient Distribution Ranges for adults are 10–35% of calories from protein, 20–35% from fat and 45–65% from carbohydrate.
